title: deadlock-batching-synthesis-wip
content:
One-line summary:
An in-production deadlock combined with unbounded per-request buffer growth in the continuous-batching path caused multiple worker pods to become unresponsive and then OOM on 2026-02-16. This doc collects initial SRE notes, a focused runbook draft, and proposed short/medium-term fixes.

Incident snapshot (short):
- Window: 2026-02-16 02:589:00 UTC (peak failure ~03:109:30).
- Symptom: sustained 95/99 latency spikes and 502/504 errors from serving frontends.
- Affected: us-west-2 model pools serving short-sequence traffic (high prefix overlap).
- Immediate mitigation: disable prune thread and reduce batch-merge aggressiveness; reroute 30% traffic to fallback model; graceful rolling restart of worker pool.

What we observed (engineer notes):
- Logs showed requests stuck in state "waiting_for_reorder" while prune_worker threads logged "acquired_write_shard". Stack dumps show reorder path blocked on scheduler::mutex while prune held shard write lock that in turn tried to update scheduler metrics (lock inversion).
- Per-pod RSS increased steadily before OOM; heap and native arena both grew. New pods did not show the same pattern until warmed.
- Autoscaler created more pods but they also hit stuck behavior once they warmed and participated in cache compaction.

Initial hypothesis chain:
1) Continuous-batching merge heuristic introduced synchronous compaction calls when merging small batches to reduce mem copies.
2) KV cache background pruning was changed to be more aggressive and to report stats by calling into scheduler telemetry (acquiring scheduling mutex).
3) Under high-frequency short-prefix requests, compaction and prune formed a cycle of lock acquisitions with inversion and exponential per-request buffering due to retry/backoff loops.
4) Memory growth eventually triggered OOMs.

Evidence gathered (commands we ran):
- kubectl -n serving exec -it <pod> -- cat /proc/<pid>/stack -> many threads show "reorder_compact() -> kv_shard_lock_write()" and others "prune_worker() -> scheduler_update()".
- pmap / proc maps -> large anonymous mappings correlated with buffer alloc traces.
- Prometheus dashboards: serving.batch.reorder_count spiked; serving.kv.prune.ops spiked earlier; serving.pod.memory.rss p99 increased for affected pods.
- Heap profiles captured with admin endpoint: allocation hotspots in reorder buffer allocations.

Immediate mitigation checklist (playbook draft):
1) Verify alert -> open incident channel and set priority P1 if 95p latency > 2x baseline and error ratio > 0.5%.
2) Identify affected pools: query /admin/pools?region=us-west-2&model=model-a filter by p95 latency and restart count.
3) If stack dumps show prune + reorder lock ordering: flip feature flag prune.enabled=false and restart worker pool with graceful drain.
4) Throttle merge heuristic: set runtime config merging.window_ms = 8 -> 16 (revert to conservative).
5) Reroute traffic: update route policy to send new requests to model-a-quant or alternate region for at least 30 minutes.
6) Observe for 30m. If errors continue, scale down pool to zero and warm new pool with prune disabled, then re-enable at low traffic.

Short-term follow-ups (owners + dates):
- Instrument per-request buffer growth metric (serving.request.buffer_bytes) and emit p50/p90/p99. Owner: Lin. ETA: 2026-03-01.
- Add lock acquisition tracing to runtime (tag locks with stable names and include owner in stack traces). Owner: Ethan. ETA: 2026-03-04.
- Add CI fuzz test that randomly interleaves prune + reorder operations to reproduce deadlock in unit test harness. Owner: Jasmine. ETA: 2026-03-15.
- Audit scheduler calls from non-scheduler threads and remove cross-subsystem sync calls. Owner: Noah. ETA: 2026-03-22.

Medium-term design proposals (Q2):
- Move KV maintenance to single-threaded actor per-shard: prune requests become asynchronous messages enqueued to shard actor so prune never holds shard lock while calling scheduler paths. Rationale: removes lock inversion entirely.
- Bounded reordering buffer with backpressure: prevent unbounded accumulation by bounding buffer size per-request and signaling upstream to reject/slowdown.
- Memory accounting: split memory categories (heap-vs-native/buffer) in metrics and alert if native/buffer > 25% of pod RSS.

Runbook: quick reference (cheat sheet for on-call):
- Indicators of this class: concurrent spikes in serving.batch.reorder_time and serving.kv.prune_time + growing pod RSS without CPU spike.
- Quick stack grep: kubectl exec -n serving <pod> -- bash -c "for f in /proc/*/task/*/stack; do grep -H "reorder_compact" $f || true; done"
- If prune thread present AND reorder blocked -> disable prune, trigger rolling restart.
- If memory growth present but no lock inversion: call admin /evict?mode=graceful then monitor.

Blameless notes + learning attempts:
- Two small changes (one in scheduler heuristics, one in cache maintenance) were merged close in time. Individually they passed unit tests but combined they produced a cross-cutting failure mode not exercised by CI.
- We need a policy: any change that touches cross-cutting sync (locks) must include a concurrency model doc and a small stress test in CI simulating background maintenance.

Open investigations (owners):
- Autoscaler behavior: why did new pods not restore capacity earlier? Investigate LB readiness vs application-level warmness and request sticky routing. Owner: Derek. ETA: 2026-03-03.
- Confirm whether forced eviction may disrupt resume tokens/session state for long-running streams; if so, add session draining to admin. Owner: Samira. ETA: 2026-03-05.

Appendix: useful links & snippets
- Stack sample (redacted):
  reorder_compact()
  scheduler::mutex::lock()
  kv_shard::write_lock()

- Quick commands:
  kubectl -n serving get pods -l pool=us-west-2-model-a -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, restarts: .status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}'
  kubectl -n serving exec -it <pod> -- curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/admin/pprof/heap > heap.prof
  # dump stacks
  for pid in $(pgrep serving_worker); do gstack $pid > /tmp/stack-$pid.txt; done

Status and next review: weekly SRE + serving-runtime sync until runbook stabilized. Postmortem doc will be produced and linked to Confluence; this WIP will be archived once all action items are closed.

Author note: keeping this intentionally concise; will expand RCA section with annotated code excerpts once devs provide diffs and deterministic reproducer.
